newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin wants flexible view of three percent target.
newsitem.headline: Jospin wants flexible view of three percent target.

text.p: French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin said on Monday that if his party won the election of May 25 and June 1 France would not enter the single currency without conditions.

He also said that the Socialists wanted a flexible view of the budget deficit goal of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), preferring to look at the criterion as a "trend" instead of a fixed figure.
"I do not want to dissolve France into Europe," Jospin told Europe 1 radio, adding he wanted a strong France within Europe.

"We should not enter the single currency without conditions...If we do not put in place an economic government facing the central bank charged with managing the European currency...that would mean that we would give up our monetary policy," he said.
Jospin added that an economic stability pact, sought by Germany and supported by the centre-right French government, would lead to member countries giving up their budgetary policy as well.
He said he wanted the southern European countries, notably Italy, to join the single European currency in the first wave.
Jospin also said his party had never said it wanted to "renegotiate" the Maastricht Treaty on monetary union.

In the same interview, Jospin said the Socialist Party would not re-nationalise privatised companies. But he said that his party would not continue the privatisation of France Telecom, Thomson/Thomson-CSF, Air France or the EDF/GDF electricity and gas utilities.
